MAJOR: `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` added in `_review_evidence` but the diff adds no `import sys` (and `subprocess` is only imported inside the `try`). If `sys` isn't already module-scope, the failure path raises `NameError` and crashes `show` — please verify.

`current_stage` blocks on any non-review stage, but docs claim "committed pre-merge gate". A failing `tests`/`precheck`/`pr`/`merge`/`delivery`/`completion` event yields "blocked at <stage>", misreporting post-merge noise as a block. Restrict to pre-merge set or fix the invariant doc.

`_review_evidence` without `review_sha` runs `architect_review gate` with no `--sha`, so the rendered "current recommendation" may come from a different review sha than the recorded event — an integrity mismatch in the exact field the AC says must be authoritative.

New function `current_stage` is new shipped product-forge logic in Python. Under the stated language rule ("new shipped logic -> Go"), this needs an explicit ruling; "edits to shipped Python" does not clearly cover a new public helper.

Every `show` now runs up to two subprocesses (2×20s timeout) synchronously. Read-path latency up to ~40s with no caching or `--no-review` escape hatch; the 60→20s cut also risks transient "cannot render" under load.
MINOR: Checklist marks review stages `[DONE]` even when the rendered recommendation is `NOT READY` — "done" and "not ready" coexist in the same flow, which is confusing for the exact case the AC cares about.
`current_stage` returns `complete` for any closed status even when `REQUIRED_AT_COMPLETION` stages are missing, masking incomplete closure (the missing list is rendered far below, easily missed).

`_parse_recommendation` accepts any all-caps tail; a foreign value ("CHANGES REQUESTED", "REJECT") is displayed unvalidated despite the documented APPROVE / APPROVE WITH ATTENTION / NOT READY contract. Add a whitelist check.
Disposition key is duplicated in code output and docs; drift risk. Consider rendering the key from one constant shared with `execution_trail_check`/`core.backlog`.
Tests only assert the ACTIONED line of the disposition key; ACCEPTED/REJECTED/SCOPE and the DEFERRED-must-cite-backlog-id rule are untested at the render level.
`_review_table` was removed/renamed; no diff updates to any caller (`execution_trail_check.py`, scripts). Confirm nothing else imported it.
NIT: Status column width 14 forces "reviewed (recommendation unavailable)" to wrap into a tall unreadable cell; consider a short code + legend.
`current` is printed twice (header and section 3) and once more in the final table; one authoritative placement would read cleaner.
`_flow_rows` dict rendering relies on insertion order; sorting keys would make output stable across producers.
A "complete" item with missing stages renders all `[PENDING]` with no `[CURRENT]` marker, so the checklist looks blank-ended.
SUMMARY: Solid direction: single ordered flow, latest-event-per-stage with a Runs audit column, review stages sourced from live recommendations instead of ingest-time statuses, and good negative-path tests. Top risks are the unverified `sys` import (crash in the error path), the "current stage" blocked-set diverging from its documented invariant, an unsourced recommendation when `review_sha` is absent, subprocess cost on every read, and a possible language-rule conflict for the new Python helper.
